hello.text: This is Puffin Rock. And this is Oona, and her little brother, Baba.

hello-again.text: Good morning, Puffin Rock! Oona and Baba are ready for an adventure.

burrow-in.text: Puffins live in burrows. A burrow is a cosy hole in the ground, dug with beaks and feet.

burrow-in-2.text: Back inside the burrow. Nice and snug.

burrow-fact.text: Puffins often come back to the very same burrow, year after year.

mama-2.text: Stay close to Baba, Oona. He is only little.

mama-3.text: Have you been to see the dandelions?

papa-1.text: Off you go exploring, you two!

papa-2.text: Watch me flap! Puffins can flap their wings four hundred times a minute!

papa-3.text: I hear Mossy has found something fun up on the rocks.

flap.text: Flap, flap, flap! Puffins beat their wings very, very fast.

baba-fly.text: Baba can't fly yet. He's a puffling: a baby puffin. So he waddles instead.

dandelion-hint.text: Dandelion clocks! Blow on them, and see what happens.

dandelions-all.text: Five dandelion clocks! The wind carries their seeds far, far away, and where they land, new dandelions grow.

dandelions-back.text: Look! The dandelion clocks are back.

may-1.text: Hello, Oona! Hello, Baba! Watch me hop!

may-2.text: May the rabbit lives in a burrow too, just like the puffins.

may-3.text: Hop, hop, hop! Can you hop like me?

mossy-hello.text: Oona! Baba! Look what I found! Wheeee!

mossy-2.text: Sit in the eggshell, and down you go!

mossy-3.text: Mossy is a pygmy shrew. One of the smallest animals on Puffin Rock.

egg-hint.text: A piece of eggshell. Just the right size for sliding.

slide-1.text: They all slide down the slope!

slide-3.text: Round and round they go. Up the rocks, and down the slide.

sea.text: The sea! Puffins dive under the waves, using their wings to swim, to catch little silver fish.

sea-fact.text: A puffin can carry a whole row of fish in its beak, all at once.

hint.text: I wonder what Oona will find over there?

swim.text: Splash! Puffins float on the sea like little boats, paddling with their orange feet.

dive.text: Down she dives! Under the water, puffins swim with their wings, as if they were flying.

surface.text: Look, Baba! I can swim like Papa!

deep.text: Down, down, down, all the way to the bottom of the sea.

baba-float.text: Baba can float too. He's too little to dive, not yet. So he bobs along on top.

fish-first.text: A fish! Puffins carry the fish they catch crosswise in their beaks, like this.

fish-full.text: Ten fish! Oona's beak is full.

fish-hint.text: Baba is hungry. Maybe Oona can catch him some fish from the sea.

fed.text: Yum! Puffin mums and dads fly out to sea again and again, to bring their pufflings fish.

baba-thanks.text: Thank you, Oona! More fish, please!

wood.text: This is the Mossy Wood. It is shady, and quiet, and everything is soft and green.

wood-fact.text: Moss grows where it is damp and shady. It is soft and springy, like a cushion.

mushroom-hint.text: Some of these mushrooms glow. Touch one, and see.

mushrooms-all.text: Five glowing mushrooms! Now the whole wood is lit up.

pond.text: The pond! Look at the lily pads. The frog is bouncing on them.

boing.text: Boing! The lily pads are bouncy!

frog.text: Ribbit! Frogs love lily pads. They sit on them in the sun, and wait for flies.

cliffs.text: The seabird cliffs. Gannets and kittiwakes make their nests on the ledges, high above the sea.

wind.text: Whoosh! The wind blows up the cliff, and lifts Oona up, up, up, just like the seabirds.

silky-see.text: Look! It's Silky the seal, resting on her rock.

silky-hello.text: Hello, Oona! Hop on my back, and hold on tight!

silky-fact.text: Seals are wonderful swimmers. Silky can stay under the water for a long, long time.

silky-again.text: That was fun! Come back any time, Oona.

shore.text: The rocky shore. Look in the rock pools: all sorts of creatures live in them.

crab.text: A crab! Crabs walk sideways. Scuttle, scuttle, scuttle!

anemone.text: A sea anemone. Touch it gently, and it closes up tight.

blowhole-hint.text: Whoosh! That's a blowhole. The waves push the water up through a hole in the rock.

tunnels.text: And look: tunnels, winding all the way under Puffin Rock!

nest.text: The nest, lined with soft dry grass and feathers. Time for a little nap.

hedgehog.text: Shh! A hedgehog, fast asleep. Hedgehogs sleep all day, and wake up at night to look for beetles and worms.

hedgehog-2.text: Sniff, sniff. He curls up into a prickly ball!

worm.text: A worm! Worms dig tiny tunnels of their own, and keep the soil soft and healthy.

warren.text: Hello, Oona! You climbed up into our warren! Meet my brothers and sisters!

rabbits-fact.text: Puffins sometimes make their homes in old rabbit burrows. So puffins and rabbits can be neighbours, underground!

marvin-hello.text: Oh! Hello, Oona. I'm Marvin. Watch my big splash!

marvin-fact.text: Otters love to play in the water. Fly up high over the pond, and let go, to splash like Marvin!

bridge.text: An old stone bridge, all covered in soft green moss.

sheep.text: Baa! A mammy sheep and her little lamb, munching the sweet grass.

bernie-1.text: Hello, Oona! This shell is much too big for me.

bernie-2.text: Hmm. Now this one's too small!

bernie-3.text: Ah! This one is just right!

bernie-fact.text: Hermit crabs don't grow shells of their own. They borrow empty ones, and move into bigger ones as they grow.

kelp.text: A kelp forest! Kelp is a seaweed that grows tall and wavy, like trees under the sea.

jelly.text: Moon jellies, drifting along with the sea. Look, but don't touch. They can sting!

whale.text: Look, far out to sea! A whale, coming up to breathe. Whoosh!

cannonball-2.text: Wow, Oona! That was an even bigger splash than mine!

climb.text: Up, up, up the roots! Come on, Baba!

branches.text: The tunnels go every which way! One goes up, and one goes down, down, down.

pantry.text: A little larder, full of seeds and nuts and berries. Whose could it be?

mouse.text: A wood mouse! Mice store seeds and nuts underground, to eat in the winter.

cave.text: A deep, dark cave. Look at the mushrooms, and all those silvery threads.

fungi.text: Fungi grow long threads under the ground, joining the roots of the plants together, like a secret web.

glow.text: Ooh! The light goes all the way along!

dunes.text: The sand dunes! Marram grass holds all the sand together, with its long, long roots.

dig-hint.text: Something is hidden in the sand. Dig, and see what you find!

dig-glass.text: Sea glass! Smooth and shiny, like a jewel!

dig-scallop.text: A scallop shell! It looks like a little fan.

dig-purse.text: A mermaid's purse! It's really an egg case. A baby dogfish grew inside it, and swam away.

dig-all.text: Three treasures from the sand! What a lucky puffin.

bog.text: A boggy place. The ground is soft and squelchy, and white bog cotton nods in the breeze.

dragonfly.text: Dragonflies! They can fly forwards, and backwards, and even stop still in the air.

falls.text: A waterfall! The water tumbles down the rocks, splish, splash, into the pool.

rainbow.text: Look! A rainbow! When the sun shines through the spray, it makes all the colours.

night.text: Night time on Puffin Rock. Look at all the stars!

morning.text: Good morning, Puffin Rock! A brand new day.

fireflies.text: Fireflies! They make their own little lights, blinking on and off.

bedtime.text: It's bedtime, my little puffins. In you come!

goodnight.text: Goodnight, Oona. Goodnight, Baba. Sweet dreams.

plankton.text: Look! At night, tiny creatures in the sea glow, wherever Oona swims.

hedgehog-night.text: The hedgehog is awake! Hedgehogs come out at night, to find their supper.

papa-fly.text: Follow me, Oona! Up, up we go!

papa-fly-fact.text: Puffins fly fast and low, flapping their wings all the way.

papa-fly-end.text: Well done, Oona! You're a real flyer now!

still-shh.text: Shh. If Oona stays very, very still...

butterfly.text: A butterfly! It's landed right on Oona's head!

bee.text: And a bumblebee! Bumblebees visit the flowers, and help them make their seeds.

rain.text: Pitter, patter. It's raining on Puffin Rock!

rain-fact.text: Puffins don't mind the rain. Their feathers are waterproof!

puddle.text: Splish! Splash! Puddles are for jumping in!

hide-start.text: Let's play hide and seek! You count, Oona!

hide-ready.text: Ready or not, here I come!

hide-hint.text: Listen! Can you hear Baba giggling?

oona-3.text: Where shall we go next, Baba?

neighbours.text: The neighbours are popping out to say hello!

footprints.text: Footprints in the sand! The waves will wash them away.

frog-fly.text: Slurp! The frog caught a fly, with its long, sticky tongue.

bunny.text: A bunny! Rabbits dig lots of holes, all joined up under the ground.

mouse-nibble.text: The mouse is having a little snack. Nibble, nibble.

pup.text: Silky's pup! A baby seal is called a pup.

talk-may-a.text: Oh, hello, Oona! Come in, come in. This old log is my favourite hiding place.

talk-may-c.text: When it rains, I sit in here and listen to the drops go pitter, patter on the roof.

talk-may-d-1.text: Ooh, clover! Is that your favourite food, May?

talk-may-d-2.text: Is that your burrow? How many brothers and sisters live in there?

talk-may-e1.text: Clover! Sweet, juicy clover. And dandelion leaves. Nibble, nibble, nibble, all day long.

talk-may-e2.text: Rabbits' teeth never stop growing. So they have to keep on chewing!

talk-may-f1.text: Oh, lots and lots! Too many to count! We all live together, in our warren.

talk-may-f2.text: Baba's my only brother. But sometimes he feels like lots!

talk-may-f3.text: Ha ha! Little brothers are like that.

talk-may-g-1.text: Can you teach me to hop, all the way up onto that stump?

talk-may-g-2.text: Look, the moon's out already. What do you do at night, May?

talk-may-h1.text: Of course! Bend your legs, and, boing! Now you try!

talk-may-h3.text: That was a very good puffin hop!

talk-may-i1.text: We come out to nibble the grass when it gets quiet, in the evening, and early in the morning.

talk-may-i2.text: Rabbits have big eyes and long ears, so they can see and hear, even in the dark.

talk-may-z.text: Come back and visit me again soon, Oona. And bring Baba too!

talk-mossy-a.text: Oona! Sit here with me. You can see the whole sea from up here!

talk-mossy-b.text: Wow. It's so big. And so blue.

talk-mossy-c.text: I come up here every day, to watch the waves, and the birds, and the clouds.

talk-mossy-d-1.text: A beetle! Mossy, is that what you eat?

talk-mossy-d-2.text: Mossy, what shape is that cloud?

talk-mossy-e1.text: Beetles! And spiders, and woodlice. I have to eat and eat, because I'm so tiny.

talk-mossy-e2.text: A pygmy shrew is so small, it has to eat nearly all the time, to keep warm.

talk-mossy-f1.text: Hmm. I think it looks like a giant fish! Or maybe a sleepy seal.

talk-mossy-f2.text: I think it looks like Baba!

talk-mossy-g.text: Oona, do you ever wish you could fly all the way across the sea?

talk-mossy-h-1.text: Look, a feather! Yes! One day I'll fly far, far away!

talk-mossy-h-2.text: No. Look, there's a burrow, just like ours. I like it here, on Puffin Rock.

talk-mossy-i1.text: And then you would come back, and tell me all about it?

talk-mossy-j1.text: Me too. Puffin Rock is the best place in the whole wide world.

talk-mossy-z.text: Oh! Is that a beetle? Bye, Oona!

talk-marvin-a.text: Oh! Hello, Oona. Do you want to sit on the bridge with me? I like to watch the water.

talk-marvin-b.text: Hello, Marvin. What have you got there?

talk-marvin-c.text: It's a pebble. A special one. Look how smooth it is. I collect special things.

talk-marvin-d-1.text: Are those special things too? Can I see your collection?

talk-marvin-d-2.text: A fish, jumping! Do you like swimming, Marvin?

talk-marvin-e1.text: Really? You want to see? Nobody ever asks! I keep it in my holt, under the tree roots.

talk-marvin-e2.text: An otter's home is called a holt. Otters are shy, and hide their holts close to the water.

talk-marvin-e3.text: Here. You can have this pebble, Oona. To start a collection of your very own.

talk-marvin-f1.text: I love swimming! Under the water, I can close up my ears, and my nose.

talk-marvin-f2.text: You can close your ears? Wow!

talk-marvin-f3.text: It keeps the water out. Otters are very, very good swimmers.

talk-marvin-z.text: Thank you for sitting with me, Oona. It's nice, having a friend.

talk-silky-a.text: Hello, little Oona. Sit beside me, and let's watch the waves come in.

talk-silky-b.text: Silky, you know everything about the sea.

talk-silky-c.text: Not everything, dear. But I have swum a very long way.

talk-silky-d-1.text: Look, a whale! Is that the biggest animal in the sea?

talk-silky-d-2.text: What are those little sparkles in the water?

talk-silky-e1.text: The blue whale. The biggest animal there has ever been. Bigger than any dinosaur!

talk-silky-e2.text: A blue whale's heart is as big as a little car.

talk-silky-f1.text: That's plankton, the smallest things in the sea. So tiny you can hardly see them. At night, some of them glow.

talk-silky-f2.text: I saw them! They sparkled when I swam!

talk-silky-g.text: Tell me, Oona. What do you like best about the sea?

talk-silky-h-2.text: Splashing in the waves, like that big one!

talk-silky-i1.text: Ha! Me too. We're both fishers, you and I.

talk-silky-j1.text: The waves are the sea's way of playing. I think it likes you too.

talk-silky-z.text: The tide is turning. Off you go, now. I'll see you in the water.

talk-bernie-a.text: Ahoy, Oona! Pull up a pebble. I've been exploring the rock pools.

talk-bernie-c.text: All sorts! Look closely, and a rock pool is a whole little world.

talk-bernie-d-2.text: Ooh, a shell! Where do you find yours, Bernie?

talk-bernie-e1.text: It is! And did you know, a starfish can grow a brand new arm, if it loses one?

talk-bernie-f1.text: The sea brings them in. When a sea snail doesn't need its shell any more, someone like me can move in.

talk-bernie-f2.text: Sometimes hermit crabs line up, biggest to smallest, and all swap shells at once, so everyone gets a better one!

talk-bernie-g.text: Now, Oona. A crab always says goodbye properly. Watch. Click, click, click!

talk-mama-a.text: Come here, my little puffin. Snuggle in. Baba's nearly asleep already.

talk-mama-b.text: Mama, will you tell me a story?

talk-mama-c.text: Of course. Which story would you like?

talk-mama-d-1.text: Look, a bit of eggshell! Tell me the story of when I was an egg!

talk-mama-d-2.text: This old leaf blew in with the wind. Tell me the story of the big storm!

talk-mama-e1.text: Once upon a time, Papa and I made this burrow. And in it, I laid one little white egg.

talk-mama-e2.text: We kept it warm for weeks and weeks. Then one morning: tap, tap, crack! Out came a fluffy little puffling. And that was you.

talk-mama-e3.text: Puffin mums and dads take turns, keeping their one egg warm.

talk-mama-f1.text: Once, a great storm blew in from the sea. The wind howled, and the waves were as tall as the cliffs.

talk-mama-f2.text: But we were safe and dry, deep in our burrow, all cuddled up together. Just like now.

talk-mama-h.text: I love you too, Oona. All the way to the moon, and back again.

talk-mama-z.text: Now close your eyes. Sleep tight, my little puffin.

talk-hint.text: What will Oona talk about? Tap something, and see!
